items.body: This album is a collaboration between the American Black-Metal and Experimental projects Sutekh Hexen (whom we already know well) and Hissing. The release comprises two lengthy tracks, originally performed live by the two bands—one in 2017 and the other in 2019. These recordings have now been reworked and refined to create “SH:HS”. What you hear seems to be primarily the result of meticulous improvisation, shaped into a form that incorporates a wide range of influences. It starts out as Dark-Ambient, quickly evolves into pure Drone, and then transforms into a truly Cinematic passage that, in turn, shifts into something considerably noisier. Growling vocals also emerge, adding to the overall sense of darkness. The second track stands out for its boundless sound manipulation and myriad effects, eventually losing itself in a relentless—and, to my ears, somewhat grating—Hardcore rhythm. “SH:HS” sounds like a musical crossroads where various genres seek an outlet, ultimately merging into a dark, cohesive whole. For me, however, it is the first track that really sticks with me. (Rating:6½). Listen to “LAX”: LAX by Sutekh Hexen & Hissing About Sutekh Hexen and Hissing Sutekh Hexen is an American experimental black metal project based in Oakland, California, originally formed in San Francisco. The band has been active for over a decade, dating back to at least 2010, and started out anonymously with three limited demo tapes that combined atmospheric black metal with noise electronics and dark ambient. Over the years its recording and live line-up has drawn on a wide cast of musicians, including A.C. Way, Demian Johnston, Joshua Churchill, Kevin Yuen, Lee Camfield, Mackenzie Chami, Ryan Jencks, Samuel Torres and Scott Miller. Sutekh Hexen’s release chronology includes the self-titled album “Sutekh Hexen” (2019, Cyclic Law), the collaborative album “P:R:I:S:M” with Funerary Call (2023, Cyclic Law/Sentient Ruin), and “Primeval” (2025, Cyclic Law/Breath Sun Bone Blood), an album built entirely from acoustic strings, percussion and wind instrumentation. Hissing is a death/black metal band from Seattle, Washington, whose members include Joe O’Malley, Sam Pickel and Zach Wise. Its discography includes the albums “Permanent Destitution” (2018) and “Hypervirulence Architecture” (2022). Sutekh Hexen and Hissing first shared a release with a split album on Flenser Records in 2017, the same year one of the two live performances reworked for “SH:HS” took place. The second performance dates from 2019. Both recordings have now been refined into the two tracks that make up “SH:HS”, released digitally and on CD via Cyclic Law.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Sutekh Hexen与Hissing两支美国乐队对两场现场录音（2017与2019年）进行重构与打磨的成果，收录了两首篇幅漫长的作品。声音从黑暗氛围起步，迅速转入纯粹的嗡鸣段落，继而演变为电影化的过渡，再滑向明显更嘈杂的噪声领域，并加入低吼式人声，强化整体的幽暗气质。第二首曲目在声音操控与效果运用上更加无边无际，最终陷入持续而略显刺耳的硬核节奏中。整体听感如同多种音乐类型交汇的岔路口，在变化中仍凝聚为统一的黑暗美学。相比之下，第一首曲目更令人印象深刻，具有更强的氛围塑造力与听觉辨识度。该作体现了两支乐队在即兴与细致编排之间的平衡，适合偏好黑暗实验声响的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Ka Baird的一次显著转向，舍弃了此前标志性的人声、合作与现场空间探索，转为完全独奏的纯律调音Rhodes电钢琴作品。通过使用纯律而非平均律，琴音的和声关系被重新校准，产生出微妙的音差与泛音变化，使每颗音符都带有更原始、更物理性的共振。整张专辑聚焦于乐器本身的声音特质与调律体系带来的听觉差异，在极简的素材中展开细腻的音色与时间层次。对于关注实验音乐、即兴传统之外的声音探索的听众而言，它提供了一种从表演性转向聆听性的深度体验，也展现了一位艺术家在个人语言上的进一步拓展。

items.body: From dub to industrial and Tanzania to Thailand, from an untitled album by an unnamed artist to a turntable album without records, our Electronic Music Preview has it all! This adventurous slate is bound to appeal to the mind as well as to the body. Site favorites such as Jónsi and Andy Bell appear in surprising categories, while newcomers make their play for the big time. One thing is sure: the dance floors won’t be empty this season. We’re halfway through our Fall Music Preview, with much more to come; our largest installment is set to appear tomorrow! Our cover image comes from Petrels’ Infangthief, covered below. Bonobo is the biggest name on fall’s electronic slate. Fans won’t have long to wait, as Distance in Static is released on September 11. As with previous efforts, the album offers a mix of vocal and instrumental cuts, the bonus being that the vocal tracks are in English, Urdu and Japanese. We’re enamored with lead cut “Drift,” and expect mainstream success (Ninja Tune). The same (safe) prophecy holds true for Chrome Sparks‘s Ball of Light, especially as the producer has roped in Khalid and Jónsi for lead single Sleeper. The languid opener is not representative of the album as a whole; for a more accurate representation, spin the club-friendly title track and then “Pleasure” (Chrome Sounds/AWAL, September 11). Nathan Fake is back, and it didn’t even take that long! The Caldera EP is a follow-up to Evaporator and the Hypercube EP from February and May (InFiné, October 23).   Bibio & Dorian Concept are releasing the expressive Answers, their first collaborate album after years of friendship. The timbres are warm and inviting, perfect for autumn (Warp, October 16). It’s only fair that we mention The Avalanches, though we’re not yet sure if the album is primarily vocal or instrumental; the sample-based Since I Met You is still one of our all-time favorite albums, and we’d love the same to be true for No Bad Memories, out October 16 and preceded by Can’t Get Over Losing You. Another sample-based artist, Odd Nosdam, is releasing a “love letter to the vinyl format.” On Patrol is packed with slow beats, obscure loops, and enthralling grooves: a crate digger’s delight. Bonus points for the cool cover art, seen right (Alien Transistor, October 23).   Is it acid? Is it jazz? Is it ambience? Is it hardcore? Yes ~ Semiratruth‘s S!M is all of these things and more, hopping genres like low fences in a wide field. A lot of ground is covered in twenty-two tracks, not one longer than 3:04 (Sooper, September 25). Space Afrika‘s Quiet Storm is a study in contrasts: featuring segments of ambience, electronics, opera, hip-hop and modern composition. The support cast is massive, each guest contributing a different aspect of a greater story. A spiritual thread runs through the recording, lifting it to a higher level (Dais, September 25). The snails seen on Carmen Villain‘s Memoira are purposeful; the album is one of “deceleration,” with trumpet, clarinet, flute, piano and strings, all filtered through sluggish beats and dub timbres (Smalltown Supersound, September 4). Post Dub Cities is the new concept album from Adriano Zanni, who wanders an unpopulated landscape and finds it rich in sound. The accompanying photos makes it seem less science fiction than recent history (Bronson Recordings, October 2). Soaked in crackle and reverb, Oblique‘s Ghost Dubs is an exercise in tension and mood. Opening single “Low Times” comes with a series of alternate mixes (Pressure, September 25).   Alien Alarms are Tuned to Different Frequencies. The album investigates a wealth of tonalities, uses creative composition to address the modern malaise of distraction. “The machine is much, but it is not everything” (PATCHWORKS, October 2). พังและแพง splits the difference between ambient and electronic on หัดขับรถ, whose title means “Learning to Drive.” The Thai producer calls the sound “dance music for introverts” (September 4). James Gorczyca also straddles the line between genres, adding a bit of modern composition on Weights of this world., whose aural presence is accompanied by a “visual world” (September 2). Les Brown‘s The One After That is the concluding part of a loose trilogy. Punchy rhythms accompany kind patterns, with a slightly cinematic lean (September 22). According to Short Span, it was “important to have Eden Aurelius‘s Entre Nous out for summer.” Close enough, as the album shimmers like the low angle of the ever-sinking sun. The further south one lives, the greater the impact will be (September 17). Supporting our theory that 2026 is The Year of Blue, Emily A. Sprague offers Cyano, drenched in blue synth and voice. There are various ways to procure the bonus tracks, including 7″ and Japanese CD; a limited edition RISO booklet is also available (RVNG Intl., October 2). Belbury Poly returns with his ninth album, Sorcery, a set of nostalgic sci-fi synth, referencing the golden 80s of sight and sound (September 25). Those who miss disco will be enamored with Narcoba‘s Pechersk. The title track could be mistaken for an instrumental by the Pet Shop Boys (Nisantashi, October 2). Loula Yorke seems always to be in a positive mood, and the upbeat nature of her personality shines through her music. Starling Sessons is filled to the gills with synth and exudes a playful tone (Truxalis, September 4).   Here’s something we didn’t expect: Infangthief and Outfangthief, a pair of interlocking albums from old fave Petrels. The drone remains intact, while the beats come hard and fast, reflecting the time spent revisiting and remixing. (Denovali, October 16). Church meets club on Music for Air, as the duo of Gamut Inc uses computer-controlled pipe organ to produce sounds more suited to Saturday night than to Sunday morning. We hold out hope that this music might find its way into a forward-thinking worship service (Karlrecords, October 16). Ride bassist Andy Bell joins harp and synthesizer duo Masal for Common Primitives, a lovely album whose rock tones set it apart from others in this article. The moods shift from placid to encouraging, often within single pieces, as new aspects of the music are turned toward the light (Sonic Cathedral, October 9). Names On Tapes offers Ayin, which celebrates the Jewish concept of “absence as potential,” the seat of creation. Clarinet, guitar and electronics emerge from the void (September 4). Then from nothing we travel to NOWHERE, found “between movement and stillness,” as PHILMS explores the liminal spaces like “That Uninspiring Beige Building” (November 17).   Slow and steady wins the race. Never rising above 121 BPMs, Philipp de Castro‘s Morferna is a lesson in restraint. “Oximoro” even includes a sound like that of a tea kettle, waiting to boil (Fala Nocturna, September 18). Peter Gall‘s Drum Seeds allows the percussion to take center stage, enhanced by synth and keys, producing a sound somewhere between jazz and electronic, with a trance-like veneer (Compost, September 4). Vintage drum machines, live drumming from Valentina Magaletti and sporadic punk-energy vocals make Holy Tongue‘s Basilikum an exciting experience. Lead single “Coca” might fit into an adventurous goth set (AD 93, October 4). One might expect to find Future Sounds of Jazz, Volume 16 in another department, but while the series honors jazz, it falls firmly into the electronic category and features exclusive tracks (Compost, September 18).   opo collects seven years of experiments on 666ridims (2020-2026), using unconventional rhythms, infusing the music with a pan-cultural flavor (Meakusma, September 3). Don’t be fooled by the opening track; Max Kutner‘s The Illustrated Interior veers from rock to glitch to percolation to prog. Infused with a sci-fi sheen, the album sounds as literary as its title (September 16). Sporting a wild cover by Kat Williams Illustrations (shown left), Ørdop Wolkenscheidt‘s concept album Stallmeister Rittich vs. the Machine takes as its starting point the 18th century lost and found poem “The Ballad of Stallmeister Rittich,” and builds a narrative around the hero’s journey: music unfolding like a narrative in verse (October 9). The slightly scary House with a Curse arrives with a silent film video and a sense of fun, the Halloween love child of Andrew Waslylk and Tommy Perman. There’s a haunted story in these grooves, perfect for the midnight hour (Clay Pipe Music, October 16). We’re digging the video for “Plastic Minds / Elastic Machines,” from Jeremiah Chiu‘s Edge Conditions; the frames flash with the percussion, and the presentation is a breath of fresh air (International Anthem, October 9). With “eight prepared turntables, four mixers, no records, six hands,” Institut für Feinmotorik is an outlier. Öd (meaning “barren” or “boring”) is anything but; these are the sounds our turntables hide from us, brought out of the shadows and into the light (Faitiche, October 9). J. Juva‘s loop-based Unclocked uses techniques invented by Steve Reich to set patterns against each other in a miasma of sound. Don’t expect an ambient record; the album is packed with beats and patterns, angular at times yet still suited for adventurous club floors (September 25). Slaylor Moon makes angular, unconventional machine music, “pushing keys, buttons, pads, or wheels.” Crisis Make Up! heads in unexpected directions, but is never random (Maple Death, October 9).   The post-industrial sound of DIKDӔDØR has evolved over time, and now includes drum machines and a power mixer. Their sound continues to be bleak and uncompromising, but now ~ perhaps ironically ~ one can dance to it. The Entertainer is released September 9 on Edelfaul. Also in this vein, A Tomb Full of Stars walks a post-apocalyptic landscape, decorating it with echoed words and the sounds of forgotten melodies, rescued from the ash. 1:When the Reflection Passes is released on Varia September 22. Fresh from Birdsong (made with birds only), Megafauna returns with an immersive, industrial, self-titled album. Voidscan appears on one track, lending the project to an even darker hue (Syrup Moose, September 25). While the music is informed by tragedy, Anthony Baldino‘s CONVEYER bleeds dramatic tension, offering not healing but catharsis, scoring the pain beat by devastating beat (BL_K Noise, September 18). After 17 years, Lauren Bousfield (Nero’s Day at Disneyland) returns to claim her throne. After influencing many splattercore sci-fi IDM artists, she hasn’t lost a step. The Grand Reopening EP drops October 16, preceded by the Mormon-sampling single ØBabylon. Beautifully harsh sounds decorate Cenizas 1era Parte, a broken beats and bass set from Lima’s XR1S, with an industrial sheen (nodo, September 10).   The fact that deep glens opened for Autechre last year opens a window into the artist’s sound. carver is intricate and melodic, while defying expectations of where the beats might land next (September 17). The beats are generous on Roel Funcken‘s Kine 3, spanning the length of a double CD. In an unusual confluence, the artist will be opening for Autechre this year. As the title implies, this is the continuation of a series that gets better with each installment (EC Underground, September 4). Machine Records is the perfect landing place for Foel, whose IDM rhythms are mysterious and dark, a reflection of difficult experiences. Gwasagaru means “scatter-disperse,” which is exactly what these beats do while dancing around a melodic core (September 4).   The clever unknown-untitled offers the double 12″ uu05 on September 18, with information revealed a week later. This way, the house-techno rhythms can be appreciated on their own, with wild speculation as to their origins. While the spelling is different from the epic poem and film, “odissiy,” the closing track on maxolydian‘s altre galassie, is meant to score the end of a journey: one that spans the galaxies and ends up safe at home (September 1). Uplift (Butterfly) is the first taste of Tom VR‘s Don’t Know How Fast I’m Moving Until I Hit Something, an upbeat set inspired by the story of koi ascending waterfalls to become dragons (Heart Somersault, September 9). Never far from our consciousness is Subsist & Faith Disciplines, who already has a trio of releases lined up for fall. First out of the gate is Not Charlie‘s Inconformista, a seemingly oxymoronic “reflective dance floor album” that somehow accomplishes the feat (September 4). Fleet offers Percussions from Space, although one should not be able to hear said percussion while in space (September 25). Sci-fi dance floors will be enamored by Cathopsis‘ Solythode, a voyage into the outer limits of the universe (Component, September 4). JØHRN offers frigid techno on Miles of Silence Between Us, using music as a metaphor for relationships (October 16). Steady, pulsing techno dominates Oscar Mulero‘s Between Two Worlds, the 199th release from Semantica paving the way for a landmark celebration (September 25). The consistently surprising Nyege Nyege Tapes returns with Jay Mitta‘s rapid-fire Kazi Kwanza, which showcases the vivid sound of the Tanzanian underground. Get ready to sweat it out, as the BPMs approach 200 on multiple occasions (September 4). The BPMs of Silvan Strauss may not be quite as fast, but they are still hyperactive; SPRINTING also boasts an international cast, primed to bring the producer’s vision to full fruition (Kabul Fire, September 4). We are really looking forward to fabric presents Max Cooper. The tracklisting blends old favorites with exclusives, along with some surprising entries. Ólafur Arnalds, Future Sound of London, Lusine and a Roly Porter remix of a Cooper track all share space in this upbeat mix (fabric, October 2). Richard Allen
items._cn_summary: 秋季电子音乐预览涵盖多张风格迥异的作品，从Bonobo的多语言人声电子、Chrome Sparks与Khalid及Jónsi的合作，到Nathan Fake的科技舞曲EP、Bibio与Dorian Concept的温暖合作专辑，以及The Avalanches的采样拼贴、Odd Nosdam的黑胶致敬之作。Semiratruth的二十二首短曲在酸性、爵士、氛围与硬核间跳跃，Space Afrika的《Quiet Storm》则融合氛围、电子、歌剧、嘻哈与现代作曲，并带有精神性线索。整体呈现电子音乐在俱乐部导向与实验探索之间的广阔光谱，涉及采样、跨风格融合与地域多样性，适合关注前卫声响与跨界实践的听众。

items.body: The Swedish sound sculptor enters the backrooms with an album of unstable electronic textures united by their uncanny, reality-warping potential It all starts with a burbling texture. The sound is quilted from what appear to be typical ambient tropes: the hum of water and droplets of static pattering against whispering ash. But things are not as they seem. The cut’s quietly droning flesh, which had seemed so familiar and clear a heartbeat before, suddenly reconfigures itself into a mimicry of traffic. A dim chord pushes through the fabric. items._cn_summary: Klara Lewis 的这张专辑以不断翻涌的噪音纹理为起点，将水声、静电滴落与低语般的灰烬混织在一起，营造出一种熟悉却可疑的环境声场。随后，原本稳定的嗡鸣突然转化为车流的拟态，暗哑的和弦如隔墙的管弦乐团调音般浮现，旋律在模糊与清晰之间缓慢生成。作品的核心在于利用细微的声音变形制造现实感的偏移，使日常声响获得某种非现实的维度。整张专辑不依赖宏大的声音叙事，而是通过对听感预期的持续干扰，构建出高度不稳定的听觉空间，值得关注的是其精密的声音设计和对环境声音潜能的挖掘。

items.body: Lawrence English The Rest Is My Ghost Lawrence English sets out to critique nostalgia's grip on the future The Rest Is My Ghost by Lawrence English Lawrence English’s recent work often engages with philosophical and political ideas. The Rest Is My Ghost is accompanied by an extended reflection on what he terms "Acid Nostalgia": a form of nostalgia stripped of lived complexity and repurposed as a political instrument, flattening history into comforting images while limiting our ability to imagine alternative futures. It is a compelling proposition, and one that promises a record concerned less with memory itself than with the ways memory can become a mechanism of control. The music occupies a familiar territory within English's practice. Vast drones, dense brass, choral voices and slowly... items._cn_summary: Lawrence English 的这张专辑围绕他所提出的“酸性怀旧”概念展开，批判一种剥离了复杂经验、被用作政治工具的怀旧形式，认为它抹平历史并限制了对alternative futures的想象。音乐上延续了作者惯用的创作路径：以广阔的持续低音、密集的铜管声部与合唱人声构成缓慢铺展的声场，在熟悉的个人语汇中推进主题。该专辑并非单纯关于记忆本身，而是探讨记忆如何成为控制机制，兼具哲学思辨与声响实验。对于关注氛围、嗡鸣与前卫电子交织的听众，这是一次值得深入聆听的声音实践，它提供了将政治批判融入聆听体验的一种方式。

items.body: For the third episode of our Musical Road to WOMEX, we travel not only in place but also in time: back to Saigon before 1975, when GI bars ran fuzzed-out rock and twist alongside Cải Lương theatres and bolero radio. That’s the era Saigon Soul Revival dug back up in Ho Chi Minh City in 2016, after a handful of musicians found a compilation called Saigon Rock & Soul: Vietnamese Classic Tracks 1968-1974 by Seattle label Sublime Frequencies, and realised nobody was playing that music live anymore. Nhạc kích động, the Western-influenced rock and soul strand of the period, had been banned outright after the war, while gentler nhạc vàng ballads survived. They started as a covers band and ended up writing most of their own catalogue instead. Ten years on, they carry it to WOMEX in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria this October. The band is Nguyễn Anh Minh on vocals, Indy Jeremy Vinh Laville on guitar and đàn nguyệt, Nguyễn Hương Bảo Hiếu on drums, Gabriel Kaouros on bass and percussion, and Đăng Nguyễn Khoa on keys, with traditional player Nguyễn Thị Hải Phượng guesting on đàn tranh and đàn bầu across their records. Their 2019 debut, Họa Âm Xưa, picked up airplay from Iggy Pop’s BBC6 show and France’s Radio FIP. Their second album, Mối Lương Duyên (2024), featured the single “Đám Cưới Nhà Em”, which went on to soundtrack a scene in HBO’s The Sympathizer. That December, the band recorded a live session for KEXP at l’Antipode in Rennes during TransMusicales. Their third album, Chốn Ta Về, releases 11 September via Saigon Supersound, folding in the T’rung bamboo xylophone and the sáo trúc flute alongside guest spots from multi-instrumentalist Đinh Nhật Minh and saxophonist Trần Mạnh Tuấn. From their WOMEX showcase, the band heads straight into a UK and Europe run: Musicport Festival in Whitby on 24 October, London’s Jazz Cafe the next night, then Bristol and Manchester, before continuing through mainland Europe to a Berlin date on 6 November. Below, the band talks about what it means to bring back music that was banned once already, and what they hope it means to a generation of young Vietnamese listeners discovering it for the first time. They also curate a playlist of the tracks that shaped their sound, exclusively for Rhythm Passport. For someone who’s never heard Nhạc Vàng, how would you describe what the band does, and what that sound felt like in the city it came from? Imagine being a teenager in Saigon, Vietnam in the late 1960s. Your grandparents are at a Cải Lương theater watching a traditional form of folk opera, your parents are singing along to a heartfelt nhạc vàng record in a typical Vietnamese bolero style, your auntie is going to a ballroom to dance the cha-cha-cha and on your way to the night market you pass by an American GI bar where a Vietnamese band is playing fuzzed out rock and twist songs for a young lively audience. All this while there is a war raging in the country with no end in sight. As a band we try to capture the essence of this period and imagine what it may have been like if the music of that time continued to develop without interruption until the present day. This music was effectively erased after 1975, when Western pop was banned and replaced. What drew the five of you to dig it back up rather than write something new, and how did you first find your way into these songs? Many classic nhạc vàng songs survived after 1975 and are popular to this day in Vietnam, but the more western influenced dance music, nhạc kích động, which were commonly in the styles of rock, surf, twist and soul were strictly banned and therefore were mostly unknown. When some of the members of SSR came across the compilation “Saigon Rock & Soul: Vietnamese Classic Tracks 1968-1974” we were blown away by the heavy raw sound and were amazed that these old songs were not being performed live to our knowledge, at least not the old versions. This inspired us to look more into such old recordings and start a tribute band to bring that energy back to the stage. You put rock musicians alongside players of the đàn nguyệt and đàn bầu, and let bolero sit next to psychedelia. What makes your version of this revival different from simply covering the originals? Though we started as a tribute band playing cover versions of these old 1960s/70s recordings and trying to really achieve that vintage sound, we eventually started making our own interpretations and ended up writing our own music entirely. In fact most of the songs on our albums are original compositions, many of which incorporate traditional Vietnamese instrumentation and fuse different styles in a very contemporary fashion. We always try to be true to our original inspiration and there are some old songs that are too good not to play, however our live shows and releases mainly consist of original material which we are happy to say has been received very positively. WOMEX is a room full of people who book, release and champion music from everywhere. Who or what are you hoping to connect with while you’re there? For us it’s an amazing opportunity to be able to perform at WOMEX and since Vietnam is not a country that is very present in the international music industry, we feel very privileged to be a part of such a globally recognised event. We do not have a specific agenda but we hope that we can make some good connections that will allow us to share our music and Vietnamese culture further across the world! You’ve built the band on raw, live shows: you’ve described the sound as descending out of the southern night sky. How does playing to a room of industry delegates, rather than a festival crowd, change the way you play? It’s hard to say because this will be our first time performing for a room of industry delegates haha. However, we have played several function gigs for embassies/consulates, hotels etc. and we always manage to connect with our audience and have them dancing by the end of the show. Your music resurrects a specific place and moment: the Saigon of the 1960s and 70s, dense and humid and electric. What’s it like to carry that sound to somewhere as far from it as a small Atlantic island, and does where you play change how it lands? Every place we play at has its own culture and vibe so it’s a pleasure for us to see how people react across the world. We are humans after all so we flow with and adapt to the energy at every show. That being said, we believe that wherever we play, it is our duty to create an atmosphere where people feel immersed in the music and energy we bring. Bringing back suppressed music is an act of memory as much as performance. What do you hope younger Vietnamese listeners, and audiences abroad who don’t know this history, take from it? We live in a very modern technological age where young people are increasingly valuing superficial entertainment and material wealth more than real culture. We hope to encourage the youth around the world to see the value in live performances and we especially wish to inspire our younger Vietnamese listeners to feel proud of their heritage, to appreciate and seek the roots of their culture. That is truly something worth valuing. Your new album Chốn Ta Về means “the place we return to.” What’s the homecoming in it, and where does the band go afterwards: more originals, more digging into the golden era, touring? Chốn Ta Về does not only refer to a literal home or country. The songs on the album tell different stories including ones of love, loss, resilience and acceptance. It’s not so much a matter of identity but a reference to finding our internal peace and our place in this world, no matter what the circumstances. If you could write a personal invitation to the people of Las Palmas to come and discover your showcase, what would it say? ¡Ahul a toda la gente linda de las Islas Canarias! It’s not everyday you get to hear a Vietnamese band that fuses traditional ethnic sounds with heavy contemporary grooves and psychedilia. We will take you on a journey like no other. ¡Dale! Let’s get loose and show us how you party in Las Palmas!   Saigon Soul Revival carry the fuzzed-out rock and soul of wartime Saigon into WOMEX 2026 in Las Palmas on 21 October   PLAYLIST: SAIGON SOUL REVIVAL X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – Saigon Soul Revival appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: “Kutsal Zeytin Halayı” traces one symbol across four thousand years: an olive branch carried in the beak of Noah’s dove, oil burning in lamps built for the Pharaohs, the same tree standing sacred on the Mount of Olives and sworn on in the Quran’s Fig Surah. BaBa Zula‘s Murat Ertel and Esma Ertel trade the lines between them, closing every turn of that history on the same vow: “I swear by that olive.” The song moves at a steady motorik pace, running the Istanbul band’s Anatolian psych roots into the dub and electronic experimentation they’ve pursued since 1996. Where the lyric’s mythology looks backward, its politics look straight at now: the band set the olive tree against what they call “corporate techno-fascism,” standing on nature’s side through every verse. It’s the first single from XXX, BaBa Zula’s new album, due on Glitterbeat on 25 September, at a tight thirty minutes and thirty seconds, the shortest and most focused record the band has made. Levent Akman, Ümit Adakale and Esma Ertel remain the same rhythm section that helped spark Turkey’s psychedelic revival three decades ago, joined here by guests İklim Tamkan on synth and organ and Eylül Güntekin on double bass. Watch “Kutsal Zeytin Halayı” HERE and pre-order XXX via THIS LINK. The post Daily Discovery: BaBa ZuLa – Kutsal Zeytin Halayı (Holy Olive Halay Dance) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: BaBa ZuLa 的新单曲以橄榄树为线索，串联起从诺亚方舟到古兰经的文化记忆，将神话叙事与对当代技术法西斯主义的抵抗并置。音乐上延续了伊斯坦布尔乐队自1996年以来的实验路径，以稳定的 motorik 节拍为基底，把安纳托利亚迷幻根源融入 dub 与电子声响，人声在男女两位主唱之间交替，最终落回同一句誓言。作为新专辑的首支单曲，作品在保持根源质感的同时呈现出更紧凑的结构，节奏组依旧是三十年土耳其迷幻复兴的班底，合成器、管风琴与低音提琴的加入丰富了层次。它既是一种向古老传统的回望，也是对当下政治环境的直接回应，适合喜欢跨界融合与地域文化表达的听者。

items.body: Review by alainPP — The album's centerpiece is undoubtedly the 'Medley Dark Ages Suite: Power and Bread / En de Nux / Time For Monsters / Ouroboros / Renaissance.' It delivers a new-millennium neo-sound?riff-heavy, energetic, and eager to tackle progressive metal head-on. It unfolds across four movements, starting with a shimmering intro featuring piano, Moog, and all the stylistic trimmings. The shift from snarling vocals against a symphonic backdrop to roaring guitars offers a refreshing change of pace. With a dash of flute, the influences are diverse?echoes of Jethro Tull in the distance and Schulze for the electronic elements. It is intense, complex, and even chaotic at times?featuring distant sirens and Floyd-esque vocoders?yet it works. The interwoven vocals of Stefano and Beatrice create the perfect synergy and depth to narrate the human dilemma regarding AI?a tale as old as time. A medieval touch emerges midway through, with delicate piano notes cascading alongside an austere violin and cinematic sheep sounds. The third quarter offers instrumental symphonic depth, leading into an electro-neo renaissance?a rock-opera finale with spellbinding vocals. It combines the velvety synth tones of yesteryear with a cutting-edge neo-prog sound, capped off by a space-diving outro that hits hard.The live set features four tracks from the latest album and one from the debut. 'Hamlet's Mill Ouverture' kicks things off with a barrage of synths, haughty vocals, and heavy guitars?delivering an epic, relentless, and hard-hitting progressive metal sound. 'Key to the Temple' begins with a distinctive symphonic style?layered arrangements and sharp riffs backing Stefano's edgy vocals?before shifting to a delicate interplay with Beatrice during the infectious chorus. This live performance sees them transition from neo-prog to neo-prog-metal?a spirited and emotional display. The sound is reminiscent of Clive Nolan's work. "C'e Casa a 30 Miglia" stands out for the delicate interplay of melancholic guitar over piano?a sugary-sweet ballad with broad appeal, driven by evocative Italian vocals. "Paths of the Sky"?an excerpt from the original 17-minute "Possessed by Time"?blends B�atrice's spellbinding vocals with Simone's tribal pads; a folk-medieval flute and Hammond organ then join in on this meltingly lovely, nursery-rhyme-like tune. Finally, "Dance of the Stars" features a swirling violin melody that feels truly starry. It has a vintage vibe that reinforces their live prowess?ensuring fans aren't just sitting in armchairs before heading back to the retirement home for the night.An album that truly warrants a comeback and offers a refreshing change of pace from standard RPI.
items._genre: neo-prog / progressive metal / symphonic rock / folk prog / electronic
items._cn_summary: 专辑以核心组曲《Dark Ages Suite》为主轴，该组曲跨越四个乐章，在钢琴、Moog、长笛与重型吉他之间展开，融合管弦乐、前卫金属、民谣和电子声响，并穿插嘶吼人声、交响背景、中世纪小提琴段落及电影化音效。男女声交织叙述围绕人工智能的人类困境，中段以细腻钢琴与冷峻小提琴营造古风，后半段进入交响化深度，最后以太空感器乐结尾。现场部分收录四首新作与一首首张专辑曲目，整体从新前卫转向更重的新前卫金属风格：《Hamlet's Mill Ouverture》以合成器与重吉他塑造史诗感，《Key to the Temple》呈现层次化的交响编曲和旋律对话，《C'e Casa a 30 Miglia》是忧郁的钢琴吉他民谣，《Paths of the Sky》融合部落节拍与中世纪长笛，《Dance of the Stars》以旋转的小提琴旋律收束。整张作品在复古合成器音色与当代前卫金属之间取得平衡，结构复杂且富有戏剧张力。

items.body: Review by progtime1234567 — It was only recently when I discovered that I really like this band. Even though I've been a fan ofprogressive rock/metal since around 2018, I only ever listened to Pawn Hearts by this band. WhilePawn Hearts is obviously a great album, I think I'm a bigger fan of this album. Van der Graaf Generator is one of those darker-ish sounding prog bands, sort of in the same vein asKing Crimson. For example, the first song "Killer", which is one of the more accessible songs bythis band, deals with themes of loneliness and death. The lyrics describe a shark that kills therest of the fish around it. I take this as a metaphor for someone who pushes everyone away fromthem, despite wanting to have relationships with the people around them. The song's introspectivelyrics are typical for progressive rock, but it is still a far cry from bands like Yes, whose themesusually revolve around literature, but can occasionally deal with darker themes (see the Yes Album). I personally think Van der Graaf Generator is one of the better progressive rock bands from the1970s. Although they never reached the same levels of commercial success like their peers Yes orGenesis, they were very influential on progressive rock and progressive metal. Similarly to KingCrimson, Van der Graaf Generator is your favorite band's favorite band. This album, along with PawnHearts and Godbluff make a solid trilogy of albums.
items._cn_summary: 乐评人认为这张专辑比乐队更知名的《Pawn Hearts》更值得反复聆听。开篇曲《Killer》以鲨鱼杀死周围鱼群的意象隐喻孤独者推开他人却渴望联结的矛盾心理，歌词带有典型前卫摇滚的内省特质，但整体氛围比同辈乐队如Yes更为阴郁。乐评指出，Van der Graaf Generator虽未获得商业上的广泛成功，却对前卫摇滚与前卫金属产生深远影响，与King Crimson同属“乐队中的乐队”。这张专辑与《Pawn Hearts》《Godbluff》共同构成乐队早期三部曲，展现了1970年代前卫摇滚中更具实验性和暗色调的创作方向，其声响设计融合了管风琴、萨克斯与戏剧化人声，区别于同期主流的交响化前卫风格。

items.body: Review by greenpete — I've never considered this one-of-a-kind record even close to what we might classify as "prog." But it's listed here on Progressive Archives (with gratitude) so here goes:Scholars of European history might recognize Balaklava (also spelled with a 'c', "Balaclava") as the name of the place where a famous British cavalry charge occurred in 1854 during the Crimean War. The poet�Alfred, Lord Tennyson immortalized it in his poem about valor,�The Charge of the Light Brigade. The truth is that this charge was an unnecessary military action, a suicidal maneuver that dissolved 40 percent of an entire brigade. Valor in suicide. Irony, like this, was a Tom Rapp specialty.The year 1968 had a similarly senseless military action going on, this one in Southeast Asia. More irony: Rapp dedicated his record to WWII soldier Eddie Slovik, the only U.S. soldier executed for desertion since the American Civil War."Some people thought (my) songs were hopeless. I was being realistic about the pain that's out there. If you say life is wonderful, people know it isn't true, but if you talk about the pain, someone will listen." (Tom Rapp, from "Crawdaddy," December 2008)"Tears are often jewel-like."The first thing that makes�Balaklava�different from other records is its unusual sleeve art. Album reproductions of paintings later became popular, but�Balaklava�is one of the first examples, and the painting chosen partially relates to the music inside. It's a reproduction of Pieter Brueghel the Elder's 16th-century, apocalyptic oil panel "The Triumph of Death," with typewriter characters of the band name and album title stamped across the top, as if this record is a dispatch being wired from the abyss below.The back cover features surreal illustrations by French avant-garde writer and filmmaker Jean Cocteau. Also, a quote from American philosopher and poet�George Santayana: "Only the dead have seen the end of war." And yet more irony: a photograph of a freckle-faced girl wearing a shy smile, with a daisy protruding from her plaid dress, and a button reading "Pearls Before Swine." (The photo was snapped at a peace rally by photographer Mel Zimmer. The girl's button actually said "Flower Power." Zimmer identifies his photo as "Molly Stewart.")So, the listener has an idea where this record is headed even before the needle strikes the wax. The packaging is deliberate and unapologetic. As Dante wrote in "The Inferno:"�All hope abandon, ye who enter here.Another striking thing about�Balaklava: the music is introduced by a ghost. The first "song" is titled "Trumpeter Landfrey," and is the actual voice and bugle call of a survivor of the Light Brigade charge, a man named Martin Leonard Landfried. With brimming pride,�Landfried announces, "I am now going to sound the bugle that was sounded at Waterloo, and sound the charge that was sounded at Balaklava on that very same bugle, the 25th�of October, 1854." Landfried's scratchy voice comes from a cylinder recording from 1890 that was reissued on a vinyl record that�Rapp owned.Landfried's bugle notes smoothly segue into the strummed guitar notes of "Translucent Carriages." Wikipedia calls this one of Rapp's "most enduring songs," a shivering tune whose title again harkens to yesteryear, and whose languid music includes ghostly background whisperings. One of them is the Herodotus quote "In peace, sons bury their fathers / In war, fathers bury their sons." Another is the Rapp quote "Jesus raised the dead / But who will raise the living?"The recurring chorus goes "Every time I see you, passing by, I have to wonder, why?" The identity of the "you" can be interpreted differently. Are they ancient carriages, perhaps Roman? Hearses? Maybe a woman? Is Rapp referring to Jesus? Or the pointlessness of war?"Images of April" burrows deeper into the murky surreal. It features vocal echoes, flute, bird songs, and even frog croaks to paint a world of desolation, where�springtime exists in�fleeting images that only memory can summon. If you're open to something strange, hypnotic, and completely different:As unconventional as is "Images of April," the next song, "There Was a Man," is totally conventional - the guitar/vocal music, that is. The words, maybe less so. They relate a story about a stranger who one day arrives in a village. The stranger has a scar on his head, "where there used to be a crown." He amazes the people by doing wonderful, magical things. Then the stranger leaves, sadly, suddenly. He has heard "the news from the war.""I Saw the World" is maybe the most passionate song on�Balaklava. Rapp pleads, with palpable emotion in his voice,�that he's seen the world "spinning like a toy," and "hate seems so small compared to it all." A melodious cello and piano passage helps boost this song to another plane.Rapp was an admirer of songwriter Leonard Cohen, and the Pearls honor him with a rendition of Cohen's "Suzanne." They supposedly recorded this song in one take, while sitting on the studio floor, in the dark, with candles burning. (Yes, very Sixties.) The hushed ambience they created must have succeeded, since this is one of the most respectfully rendered versions of this acclaimed song. Other titles include "Guardian Angels" and "Lepers and Roses," both of which further the odd, time-frozen quality of�Balaklava. At the end of the record, there's another vintage 1890 recording, this one of Florence Nightengale, who oversaw the nurses during the Crimean War. She prays that her Balaklava "comrades" will all return "safe to shore." The record trails off with Trumpeter Landfried's opening again.�It's a reminder that everything is a circle, that everything "comes back again,"�both love and hate.While not a perfect record - it loses steam at the very end - and certainly not for every ear,�Balaklava's�best moments�overflow with�a perceptiveness, mystery, and beauty not usually occurring in rock music. Today, we hear the word "alternative," which means "different" or "unconventional," applied to�a certain style of music (for the sake of convenience, branding, and marketing).� But Pearls Before Swine's�Balaklava�defines the word alternative.� There's�not another record like it.Even more, the record is a unique and fervent indictment of the idea that warfare is some kind of glorious endeavor. It is music with meaning.�But unlike most anti-war artists of the Sixties - idealistic and well-meaning, but who relied on anthems or derivative platitudes about peace and love - Tom mRapp used irony, surrealism, and religious and historical allusions to present his worldview. He drew from a war in 1854 to indict a war of 1968, which still resonates today.(4 stars instead of 5 only because it's not "prog" and spirit this intense could never sustain a full LP)

items._cn_summary: 这张发行于1968年的专辑以克里米亚战争中的巴拉克拉瓦战役为概念核心，呼应同时代的越战与反战情绪。开篇直接使用幸存者Martin Leonard Landfried的真实号角录音，形成历史与当下的对照。乐评指出其封面采用勃鲁盖尔画作《死亡的胜利》，并配以诗人丁尼生关于轻骑兵冲锋的诗句，整体包装充满文学与视觉艺术指涉。音乐上以民谣为基础，融入迷幻与前卫实验元素，打破当时摇滚唱片常规。专辑献给因逃兵被处决的Eddie Slovik，体现出对体制性牺牲的质疑。乐评认为这张唱片并非传统意义上的前卫摇滚，但其独特的艺术构思、历史采样与氛围营造，使其成为1960年代后期极具独创性的作品。

items.body: Thirteen of the fourteen songs are already out; the running order is the news. Mycelium Sky, the one-man dark psychedelic industrial rock project of US musician Jacoboon (Jacob Reed), release the debut album “Hello World” on Saturday 5 September 2026 through the project’s own label Mindstorm Unlimited LLC. The album is digital only, runs 69 minutes and 17 seconds, and adds one previously unreleased track, the closer “Questions Remain”, to the thirteen singles issued between 31 January and 14 August 2026. The most recent of those, “Here We Fxn Go”, is on Spotify now. The project makes no secret of how the record was built. Its press page states: “Lyrics come first, written by hand. Music is generated with Suno; videos are grown […] with Neural Frames; structure, selection, and final cut stay human.” The credits list Jacoboon for lyrics, concept, direction and edit, Suno for the music, Mixea for mastering and DistroKid for distribution; the videos come from that same AI video platform, except “Asking Questions” (made with Sora) and “Welcome to Earth M.F.” (Kling). One lyric is the exception: the words to “Roots on the Glass” were written by the AI, and the record credits it as such. “My Country” builds on two public-domain texts, Samuel Francis Smith’s 1831 “America” and A. G. Duncan’s 1843 abolitionist rewrite from “Anti-Slavery Melodies”. Mycelium Sky mix mechanical atmospheres, ritual-style lyrics and rock songwriting, and name Tool, A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Puscifer and darkwave as their reference points. Tracklist and mirror structure of ‘Hello World’ The fourteen tracks are sequenced as seven pairs that fold around a break between tracks 7 and 8, with each song in the second half answering its counterpart in the first: 1 with 14, 2 with 13, and so on. Jacoboon says the structure was found rather than designed: the album was thirteen tracks deep when one change to the running order locked the fold, moving “Lie to Me” from track 2 to track 5 and sending “Questions Remain”, until then track 8, to the end to answer the opener. The pivot pairs “Safety in Solitude” and “No Escape”, two songs the project describes as performing the same act with opposite outcomes. The running order, with single release dates: 1. “Asking Questions” (31 January), 2. “First Impression” (31 January), 3. “Roots on the Glass” (31 January), 4. “Option 2” (27 February), 5. “Lie to Me” (31 January), 6. “Fall in Line” (20 March), 7. “Safety in Solitude” (10 April), 8. “No Escape” (1 May), 9. “My Country” (25 May), 10. “Welcome to Earth M.F.” (12 June), 11. “The Misunderstood” (3 July), 12. “Strange but True” (24 July), 13. “Here We Fxn Go” (14 August), 14. “Questions Remain” (5 September). “Lie to Me”, “Fall in Line”, “Welcome to Earth M.F.” and “Here We Fxn Go” carry explicit tags. Pre-saves run through DistroKid’s HyperFollow page, and the singles are on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and iHeartRadio, among other services. About Mycelium Sky Mycelium Sky is the solo project of Jacoboon, who writes the lyrics and concepts, directs the AI tools and makes the final cut, and releases the results on his own Mindstorm Unlimited LLC. The project’s first chapter was the music video for “Asking Questions” in December 2025, followed by the first four singles on 31 January 2026 and a further nine through 14 August. A glowing red question mark recurs across every cover and video. Alongside the songs, the project runs the Tone Garden, a generative ambient instrument tuned in just intonation, on its website. The project’s press contact is handled by AI assistants that identify themselves as such; Jacoboon answers in his own name on request. “Hello World” on 5 September 2026 is Mycelium Sky’s first album and the first time the fourteen tracks appear in their mirrored sequence.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Mycelium Sky的首作，采用AI协作模式：歌词由人类手写，音乐由Suno生成，人类负责结构编排与最终选定。十四首曲目按镜像折叠排列，前后半部分一一对应，形成七对互文关系。作品融合机械质感、仪式化歌词与摇滚创作，并参考了Tool、Nine Inch Nails、darkwave等脉络。数字发行，包含一首未发表新曲。整张唱片在创作流程与结构设计上体现出明确的实验意识，其AI与人类分工的方式也为工业风格提供了新的生产范式。

items.body: For this new EP, Serbian producer Goran Alavux has teamed up with the Dutch label New York Haunted. It features four tracks that quickly immerse the listener in Alavux’s brand of Dark-Techno. Two of the tracks are hard and dark, at times interwoven with Industrial sounds and occasionally infused with a touch of EBM. In my opinion, these are the stronger tracks. The other two tracks don’t sound bad, but they are a bit too repetitive for my taste and lack the same menacing quality. Alavux always has something to offer, consistently combining high productivity with quality. (Rating:7). Listen to “M 5.3”: NYH404 03 Alavux – M 5.3. by New York Haunted About Alavux Alavux is the main recording alias of Serbian producer Goran Alavuk, who also records as Solaris Path. Discogs lists his releases from 2008 onwards on labels including Twilight 76 Records, Vocode Records, Bass Agenda Recordings, Diffuse Reality, Bunker Records and his own 0ktag0n Records, where the “Underground Is Resistance” series appears. Side-Line reviewed Polar Light on Adriatiko Recordings in January 2026 and Underground Is Resistance on 0ktag0n Records in February 2026. “Illusions” was released by New York Haunted on 28 May 2026 as a download. The four tracks are “Illusions”, “Aerial”, “M 5.3.” and “Mutatio”. No production credits are listed on the Bandcamp page and the EP has no Discogs entry at the time of writing. It is the third Alavux release reviewed on Side-Line in 2026.

Gerry Hemingway leads a band of globe-trotters: German multi-reedist Frank Gratkowski whose recorded in the US often; pianist Izumi Kimura based in Ireland; Swiss bassist Christian Weber who’s recorded on three continents, crossing paths along the way with Yanks Oliver Lake, Ellery Eskelin, Nate Wooley, and Russ Johnson; Gerry himself, based in Lucerne since 2009.

In many ways Hemingway’s contemporary music mines his time in Anthony Braxton’s wondrous 1985-1993 quartet. The leaping staccato melody with asymmetrical phrases near the top of the 36-minute “Bau 4 Assembly” is one marker; another, the way that loose suite and the 23-minute “Slivers” use long improvised sections to tie together occasional scored episodes – not that Braxton was alone in that. And Braxton’s quartet prompted Hemingway’s duo with bandmate Marilyn Crispell, prefiguring his duo with Kimura in recent years.

On the CD, a six-minute Hemingway-Kimura improvisation is sandwiched between the long pieces, but I tend to cue up that “Third Story Variation” first, for its unbeatable interplay. The pianist and drummer catch and ride the same pulse, leaving plenty of air but also knowing how to fill various spaces along the way. Their timbral senses are fully compatible: her under-the-hood preparations tilt her sound drumward. They’ll set up a slow groove together, then she’ll use her other hand to play against it. It’s all very attentive and effective.

The longer pieces credited to Hemingway unfold like narratives, with discreet episodes, varied pacing, subgroup subplots, ways to build and dispel tension. “Slivers” is for trio, minus piano, Gratkowski leading off on squawky bass clarinet, tracked by Weber’s bass; the time feel is notably looser than the duo’s. A few minutes in, bass clarinet exits, and Frank’s re-entrance on disembodied wispy alto is placed just right: an instant orchestrator’s decision. Later there’s a section for low bass clarinet and arco bass in frictive unison under free drum rustle – suggesting Braxton’s love of the sub-basement, and the flexible trio dynamic of Gerry’s early/longtime vehicle BassDrumBone. But “Slivers” does slack off a bit between the scored tentpoles. There are times you wish the drummer would apply a firmer hand in a what-would-Billy-Higgins-do kind of way. One of Gerry’s signatures at the traps is a free-swinging–arms sense of relaxation, hitting the skins as if on the rebound, with some hits maybe dropped or delayed in transit. In the closing minutes, and on the closing theme, he can come off like someone who thinks he’s swinging harder than he is.

All four assemble for “Bau 4 Assembly” which makes up the bulk of the program. The venue Bau 4 in Altbüron, Switzerland was founded by folks in the timber business, and is located in their commercial compound. In tribute, Gerry and company play or use as beaters wood scraps retrieved from the workshop, notably heard around 10 minutes in, on a fast irregular clacky and texturally light colloquy which develops into something like pointillism with a groove (no small achievement) before flute and pedal-down piano soften things up. But not for long; in very short order, a scrapwood and piano gamelan. Midway, there’s a long-tone chapter with clarinet, and Gerry singing wavery lines into his cymbals or (says here) through metal objects, an odd effect he just about pulls off. (There’s a little Robert Wyatt in his vocal wah-wahs.) The composer and the quartet cover much ground. Elsewhere, a slow line’s melodic contours are subtly mirrored by the drums.

We won’t catalog every change-up or chapter, but near the end there’s a free-jazz blowout whose presence feels like checking a box – which is not to overlook Frank’s rapid multiphonic growls. (He’s got a great command of altissimo and pressurized reed textures.) Then they break into a loose brisk tempo, to frame that free-jazz energy. It arrives just where a non-drummer’s band would place a climactic the drum solo. Then a feint toward the Braxtonian head from half an hour earlier. A few staccato hits end things without a big fuss.

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Gerry Hemingway与三位国际即兴乐手的合作，包含两首长篇作品和一段鼓与钢琴二重奏。乐评指出，音乐延续了Hemingway在Anthony Braxton四重奏时期形成的创作思路，在松散即兴与记谱段落之间来回切换，以即兴桥段串联起结构化的片段。专辑中使用了从木材工坊收集的木料作为打击乐器，赋予特定段落独特的敲击纹理。二重奏展示了钢琴与鼓之间高度默契的互动，音色与节奏相互呼应；而三首重奏则更强调低音区的摩擦与自由律动。乐评也提到，某些长段落中间的松弛感较为明显，鼓手的处理并非始终紧凑。整体上，这是一张体现即兴传统与当代创意的现场录音，展现了跨国际乐手间的灵敏对话。

items.body: Embrace Storms is a new solo work from James Murray. Consisting of two long-form sound collages, listeners will find Murrays’s music, like much of the planet, to be in a state of conflict, the middle of a prolonged storm. Opener ‘In Your Head’ contrasts and compliments the closing piece ‘In Your Heart’, as one cannot live without the other. Embrace Storms is the first multi-format split release between London’s Slowcraft Records and Milan’s KrysaliSound, two independent labels from two different nations with one goal in mind: a dedication to pursuing original, minimal, and unclassifiable music through a gorgeous set of limited editions. At first, Murray’s music resists the storm, refusing to accept its reality, only to later trust the process. Acceptance produces calm, but it’s hard to remain calm when normality snaps and everything is swept away. When the mind refuses to confront, tones are left to chaotically spin, almost losing their balance with the rapid oscillations and rising dynamics. Apart from these elements, the music remains relatively calm. Even when something undesirable hits the fan, it seems that Murray can close his eyes, calm the section, and continue on. There’s no panic or a reflexive decision. Embrace Storms doesn’t turn to look the other way. It embraces the fight, knowing that it’ll come out all the stronger, a development of character that can only be gained by going through the twister, and sometimesslogging through the sludge of surging floodwater. This storm has been growing for years, delivering a steady, soul-bruising rainfall instead of an instant downpour. Of the two, ‘In Your Heart’ is the feeler and not the thinker. Introverted notes cycle back in on themselves until they are pulled into the heart of the music, carried into a tornado-like funnel that spins in the centre of the track. They are kept there, to be stored up and used as motivation and encouragement when things seem difficult. Gold is refined in the fire. It’s time to face the music and dance. www.slowcraft.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 《Embrace Storms》由两首各占一面的长篇幅声音拼贴构成，开篇《In Your Head》与结尾《In Your Heart》互为对照与补充。音乐像一场持续多年的风暴：时而是快速振荡、几乎失去平衡的混乱音层，时而又回到相对平静的段落，呈现拒绝、承受再到接纳的心理过程。第二首更偏向内省，循环内旋的音符仿佛被卷入龙卷风般的中心，被储存为日后面对困境时的动力。作品由伦敦Slowcraft与米兰KrysaliSound联合发行，以限量实体形式推出，体现两家独立厂牌对原创、极简、难以归类声音的共同取向。

items.body: And your night is your shadow — a fairy-tale piece of land to make our dreams… This emotionally gargantuan release from the quintessentially viable and omnipresently reliable Sub Rosa starts on an unsettlingly serious nod – a feeling of relinquished grief persists throughout the album that feels like poisonous apples falling from a tree. The ever present quaintness of the sounds sourced are delightfully, obliquely measured, drawing comparisons in lighter waters with Three Cane Whale and Merzbow at the bombastic arrythmia end. What is most amazing is this release is all the work of Oiseaux-Tempete… The palette is so broad and paints a deep masterstroke while your breath flows along with it at varying tempos of pace and intensity. There are scraped bowls, field recordings of a “who, what, when, where” nature. There are brazen electric guitars in the vein of Jesu halfway through. Indeed, it is best known as electronics. I have no disappointments with the release; the record is a smooth ride through international music, especially Middle East flavoured flora and fortune. There is a lot of keeping to the electroacoustic traditional style. And the most important thing in life is good, and there is plenty of it here. While the repertoire for Sub Rosa could have a sub menu for less likely music, and something from the aether to defy logic, cohesive connectors are essential to victory. The meaning here, exemplified. www.oiseaux-tempete.com
items._genre: electroacoustic / experimental / electronic / field recording / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以电声音乐为基底，融合实地录音、刮擦碗具的细碎声响与中途出现的失真电吉他，营造出介于静谧与轰鸣之间的宽广动态。整体氛围带有明显的哀悼感，如同毒苹果坠落般 unsettling，但声音取材又保持一种精致而错落的平衡。中东色彩的音乐元素贯穿其中，使作品在 electroacoustic 传统之外延展出地域性的听觉想象。Sub Rosa 作为发行方保证了其独立与小众的取向，专辑在实验声响与可听性之间维持了流畅的叙事感，以国际化的音乐语汇构建出一个既熟悉又陌生的声音景观。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了十三个比利时创新乐团在帕克修道院内的录音，修道院的静谧与古石空间成为贯穿全作的隐形主角。音乐以器乐为主，从斯洛文尼亚小提琴家对罗马尼历史的演绎，到受 Django Reinhardt 启发的摇摆曲，再到黎巴嫩-比利时三重奏融合地中海与阿拉伯声响的乌德琴作品，风格跨度极大。手风琴与巴洛克式室内乐、中世纪元素、喉音甚至爵士低音提琴与鼓组并置，形成丰富而连贯的声响景观。制作团队利用修道院的自然混响捕捉温暖音色，使整张专辑既充满意外转折，又保持统一的冥想气质。它适合听众在安静环境中细细品味，尤其吸引对世界音乐融合、室内乐编配和特定空间录音感兴趣的乐迷。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka与班杜拉演奏者Alina Kuzma共同领导的全女性组合Daughters of Donbas录制，聚焦俄罗斯从乌克兰东部劫走约两万名儿童的战争罪行。曲目混合传统歌谣与原创作品，编制以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉和钢琴，并由乌克兰与加拿大两地乐手共同参与；其中一位成员Lisa来自马里乌波尔，曾是被劫儿童之一。乐评特别提到《Foreign Land》改编自一首关于外出帮佣女孩的传统民歌，将历史遭遇与今日被劫儿童相连，Marichka的演唱温柔克制；而由Alina Kuzma领唱的《Rusalka》则转向粗粝激烈的表达。乐评人刻意先不读歌词说明，仅以音乐本身判断，认为它在任何标准下都足够有力，随后读到歌词翻译时更深受触动。

items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.
items.label: Cool Waters
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由德国出生的打击乐手Sven Kacirek与肯尼亚歌手Ogoya Nengo及Olith Ratengo合作完成，是内罗毕厂牌Cool Waters的首张发行。83岁的Nengo带来肯尼亚dodo传统的深厚歌唱经验，与Ratengo的人声呼应形成根源纽带；Kacirek则以Buchla合成器、手 percussion 和套鼓驱动整体声响。不同于简单的传统加电子拼贴，乐曲通过层叠的合成器复节奏逐渐浮现，如《Bara》从生硬的重复音型过渡到有机融合；《Sarah》则在人声高潮处渗入失真质感。评论强调这类音乐虽被冠以folktronica标签，但更关键的是其全球化视野与非洲根源之间保持的深度联系，传统并未被技术覆盖，反而在电子语境中显露出先锋性与古老感的交融。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比1970-80年代的Puxa音乐，展现了这个小岛屿国度在非洲葡语区音乐版图中的独特声音。Puxa本身融合了来自前葡属非洲殖民地的多种节奏元素，同时受到加勒比地区音乐影响，内含merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等成分，但已形成本地化的律动语言。多把吉他的交织与呼应、主唱与和声的紧密应答，构成歌曲旋律框架的核心。曲目如《Sossegado》呈现紧凑的吉他连复段与套鼓的张力，《Sono sô ku’ dé tôma》等则在低音与键盘退出后，让鼓手和吉他驱动出更具身体性的节奏，显示出现场延伸数小时的感染力。独立厂牌Bongo Joe的挖掘让这些罕有录音重新面世，既呈现了非洲黄金年代的音乐生态，也记录了边缘地区被忽视的创作能量。

items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items.label: Songs of Compassion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以非线性的前卫音乐结构为核心，钢琴在前后景中游移、错位与叠加，配合弦乐、木管、合成器音墙和金属质感声响，构建出反常规和声运动的听觉体验。歌词由诗人与音乐作家撰写，兼具诗意与当代政治性，如《Pale Wanderer》探讨威权体制下的共谋，《Charlottesville》直指种族主义事件，延续了1960年代抗议歌曲的传统。人声以深沉而清醒的姿态融入哲学化的词句，旋律如意识流般起伏，不遵循传统调性，而是以词意为核心驱动。整体氛围既有实验音乐的疏离感，又带有冥思性的当代古典质地，适合偏好非调性、模块化结构及声音装置般聆听体验的听众。
